---
title: Themes
description: A theme is a package that renders your site's pages from the CMS's content, with no code in your app beyond one route.
---

A theme turns content into a site. It is a package you name in `tansy.config.ts`, and it renders the
pages for the collections' URL patterns: lists, single records, search, and whatever else it
declares. Your app keeps one route for the site, and the theme does the rest.

```ts title="tansy.config.ts"
import { defineCms } from "tansy/config";
import { magazine } from "@tansy/theme-magazine";

export default defineCms({ theme: magazine() });
```

The same theme package renders a headless front end over the API, so a site on its own domain or
its own deployment needs no second implementation.

  <Card title="Storefront" href="/docs/themes/storefront" description="The Shop plugin's pages redesigned, styled with Tailwind compiled inside the theme." />
  <Card title="Dispatch" href="/docs/themes/dispatch" description="A newsletter's site: the sign-up form up front and posts as numbered issues." />
  <Card title="Academy" href="/docs/themes/academy" description="A school's site for the LMS: the catalogue, course pages and the plans that open them." />
</Cards>

`@tansy/theme-blank` is a starting point with no opinions, and `@tansy/theme-blog` a small
worked example. Both are in the repository under `themes/`.
